# Results — Study 200 (ROE-Quality) on real EDGAR tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Signal: **return on
equity** (NetIncomeLoss / lagged StockholdersEquity), cross-sectionally winsorised
at 1%/99% per year. Universe: S&P 500 names from shared EDGAR cache. Firms with
non-positive lagged book equity excluded. Reporting lag: fiscal-year y fundamentals
→ calendar-year y+1 returns. Window: **2009–2025 (17 years)**. As-of **2026-06-15**.*

**Survivorship-bias caveat**: the EDGAR cache covers **current** S&P 500 members
projected backwards. Every firm in the panel survived to 2026. All results are
upper bounds in magnitude — the true live edge is weaker, and any direction reversal
would be even stronger in magnitude on a survivor-free panel.

## ROE quintile returns (2009–2025, forward 1yr)

Signal constructed from EDGAR fundamentals for fiscal year y; forward return = calendar-year y+1.
All quintile returns are equal-weight within the quintile. "Hedge" = Q5 (high ROE) − Q1 (low ROE).

| Quintile | Label | mean/yr | Sharpe | HAC *t* | Hit rate |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Q1 | low ROE | **+22.1%** | +0.78 | +7.04 | 82% |
| Q2 | | +17.2% | +1.00 | +6.45 | 82% |
| Q3 | | +19.0% | +1.02 | +6.44 | 82% |
| Q4 | | +17.3% | +0.84 | +6.11 | 82% |
| Q5 | high ROE | **+17.1%** | +0.73 | +7.78 | 76% |
| — | EW market | +18.1% | +0.90 | +9.82 | 82% |
| **hedge** | **Q5 − Q1** | **−5.0%** | −0.42 | **−1.48** | 35% |

**Key finding**: the quality premium predicted by the literature is **absent** on this
survivorship-biased S&P 500 panel. The hedge (high-ROE minus low-ROE) is **−5.0%/yr**,
HAC *t* = **−1.48** — the wrong sign of the theory, and below the inference bar (|t| < 2).
Low-ROE firms actually outperform high-ROE firms by a meaningful (if noisy) margin.

## Excess returns vs equal-weight market

| Group | Excess vs mkt | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| High ROE (Q5) | **−1.0%/yr** | −0.94 |
| Low ROE (Q1) | **+4.0%/yr** | +1.58 |

High-ROE firms underperform the market by ~1%/yr (not significant); low-ROE firms
outperform by ~4%/yr (not significant at 2-tail, but directionally opposite the theory).

## Random-portfolio null distribution

To rule out "any concentrated subset beats the market" as explanation, we compared the
high-ROE portfolio's excess return against 500 random portfolios of the same size drawn
from the same universe each year:

| | |
|---|---|
| Random control mean | ~0%/yr |
| Random control std | ~4.2%/yr |
| High-ROE portfolio excess | −1.0%/yr |
| Fraction of random portfolios *below* high-ROE | ~40% |

The high-ROE portfolio does **not** outperform random. It falls *below* the median
random draw — confirming that ROE carries no positive signal in this panel.

## Head-to-head: ROE vs Gross Profitability (Novy-Marx 2013)

GP/Assets (gross profit / total assets) is theoretically a cleaner quality signal.
On the same universe and horizon (2009–2025, restricted to the 207 tickers with
GrossProfit data):

| Signal | Q5 excess vs mkt | HAC *t* | Hedge (Q5−Q1) | Hedge *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| ROE (this study) | −1.0% | −0.94 | −5.0% | −1.48 |
| GP/Assets (Study 122 comparison) | −2.5% | −0.89 | +2.6% | +0.62 |

Neither signal produces a positive, significant quality premium on this panel. Both
point in directions inconsistent with the "quality" narrative: high-quality firms
(by both measures) **do not** earn higher forward returns in the S&P 500 over
2009–2025 once survivorship bias is named.

The hedge is positive in only 6 of 17 years (35% hit rate). Large negative spreads
dominate: 2011–2015, 2022, 2024–2025. No persistent outperformance of high-ROE firms.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Hedge HAC *t* = −1.48 (wrong sign), high-ROE Q5 excess vs market
  −1.0%/yr (*t* = −0.94); the quality premium is absent and directionally reversed.
  Panel is survivorship-biased (upper bound on magnitude), so if anything the true
  ROE signal is even weaker. Neither ROE nor gross profitability shows a significant
  positive quality premium over 2009–2025 on this universe.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Negative hedge with no statistical foundation; transaction
  costs (rebalancing annually across ~50–70 names per leg) further erode the
  already-negative point estimate. Not investable.
- **ROE is "priced"?** The ROE-quality signal is fully priced into the S&P 500 survivor
  universe — high-ROE names that made it into the index have already been bid up.
  Any future edge would require a broader, survivorship-clean universe and careful
  factor-model neutralisation (size, beta, sector) not present here.
